name: Budgets and Allowable Costs
title: Budgets and Allowable Costs
answer: Budgets and allowable costs in AI research grant proposals cover direct costs such as compute time, data acquisition, personnel, equipment, and indirect costs or overhead. They define which expenses a funder will reimburse and under what conditions. For AI work, this often includes cloud computing credits, GPU clusters, data licensing, and software subscriptions. The scope also includes cost sharing, matching funds, and in-kind contributions where required.

sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: Budget infrastructure refers to the financial and administrative systems used to build, track, and justify budgets. This includes grant management software, institutional finance systems, and cost accounting standards. In AI research, budget infrastructure also covers cloud provider pricing models, on-premises hardware depreciation, and data storage costs. These systems must align with funder rules on allowable, allocable, and reasonable costs.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Budget development typically starts with a work plan and a breakdown of activities into cost categories. Researchers estimate compute hours, data volumes, and personnel effort, then apply current rates from vendors or institutional schedules. Allowable costs are checked against the funder's cost principles, such as federal uniform guidance or private foundation policies. Justification narratives explain why each cost is necessary and reasonable for the proposed AI work.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Budget governance involves institutional review of proposed costs, compliance with funder terms, and audit trails for expenditures. Risks include cost overruns, disallowed costs, and misalignment between budget categories and actual spending. Provenance for budget figures comes from vendor quotes, published price lists, salary scales, and historical project data. Funders may require documentation to support each line item and may disallow costs that lack clear justification.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Budgeting for AI research is moving toward more granular tracking of compute and data costs as usage-based pricing becomes common. Funders are increasingly asking for separate line items for model training, inference, and data curation. There is also a shift toward standardized cost reporting for reproducibility and comparison across projects. Some funders are exploring pre-approved cloud provider rates and shared research infrastructure to reduce administrative burden.
